text:
leah_y: heads-up — found a weird duplication/fallback interaction in the sampleapp when using the retrofit suspend adapter + OkHttp on Android 16. Not the same as the streaming-replay bug; this one is about our fallback policy (switching to a cheaper model endpoint) triggering an extra POST. Repro + logs below.

omar_b: hmm. fallback policy as in our SmartRouting that retries a request against a cheaper model on 503/latency?

leah_y: yeah. flow: app POST /v1/generate -> server returns 500-ish transient -> SmartRouting interceptor tries fallback to a smaller model endpoint by building a new request and proceeding. With coroutine adapter v2, we see two POSTs reaching the fallback endpoint sometimes. It looks like the original Call isn't being canceled before interceptor proceeds with fallback clone, so both calls run. Happens more on Android 16 emulator with aggressive network flaps. Logs: 

```
2026-04-02T10:05:01.001Z D/OkHttp --> POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate (model=large)
2026-04-02T10:05:01.320Z D/OkHttp <-- 502 https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate (model=large)
2026-04-02T10:05:01.321Z I/SmartRouting: trying fallback model=small
2026-04-02T10:05:01.450Z I/Network: flaky link detected, reconnecting
2026-04-02T10:05:01.670Z D/OkHttp --> POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate (model=small) (fallback)
2026-04-02T10:05:01.671Z D/OkHttp --> POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate (model=small) (duplicate)
```

leah_y: both fallback requests have the same idempotency key header (we add X-Redwood-Idempotency) but the server accepted both since the key was only set at the SmartRouting interceptor level and the original request got cloned with a different header order? Not sure. The server log shows two distinct requests.

sam_k: curious. Two possible places to look: 1) how the Call is cloned by retrofit/coroutines — a cloned Call created by the adapter might be enqueued while the interceptor's fallback path also enqueues, resulting in two in-flight calls; 2) idempotency semantics: server dedupe usually depends on exact header value + maybe a signature. If header order changed or the idempotency middleware saw different canonicalization, dedupe fails. Did you verify the idempotency header value is identical bytes?

leah_y: I pulled the low-level wire dump and the header values match exactly. But the first fallback attempt includes chunked encoding and the second is short-lived and arrives after a reconnect; server treats them as separate because the first had a different content-length metadata (unknown) when received. So server couldn't dedupe.

omar_b: this is getting subtle. Solution space: A) ensure the original Call is canceled before we initiate fallback clone (so only one active request exists), B) make SmartRouting use a single-flight wrapper so only one fallback attempt is in-flight, C) attach a server-side idempotency token that is canonicalized and accepted even if connection semantics differ. Short-term I think (A) + (B) in SDK is reasonable.

sam_k: agree. For (A) you can call call.cancel() on the original OkHttp Call before proceeding with fallback. But with suspend adapter v2, you need to access the underlying Call object; ensure the Call isn't recreated by the adapter on resume. For (B) a single-flight AtomicReference or mutex around fallback attempts keyed by request fingerprint would avoid dupes. Also add a note to onboarding docs about retry/fallback + suspend adapter interactions.

leah_y: implemented a small change in the SmartRouting interceptor: before spawning the fallback proceed, we call response.request.tag(OkHttpCallTag::class.java)?.okhttpCall?.cancel() when present (we added a helper tag that stores the Call on creation). That reduced duplicates in stress runs on Android 16 from ~30% to ~1%.

omar_b: nice. We should be careful exposing internal Call handles via tags, but for SDK internals it's ok. Long-term we should avoid relying on tag plumbing and instead add an SDK-level helper that wraps execute/proceed + fallback with cancel-on-fallback semantics. Also update server dedupe to canonicalize idempotency tokens regardless of transfer encoding.

sam_k: also check dispatcher settings: if dispatcher.maxRequestsPerHost is low and retryOnConnectionFailure=true, the dispatcher can re-enqueue clones unexpectedly. Recommend documenting default dispatcher settings in the Android SDK guide and maybe providing a preconfigured OkHttpClient builder that sets safer defaults for mobile (e.g., retryOnConnectionFailure(false) for upload/generate calls or adjustable).

leah_y: I opened a PR with three changes: 1) SmartRouting: cancel original call before fallback and single-flight guard, 2) SDK: add FallbackGuard utility + sample usage in sampleapp, 3) docs: onboarding note about suspend adapter v2 + fallback/retry interactions and recommend idempotency header canonicalization on server. See RED-DEVEX-4011.

devex-bot: Created issue RED-DEVEX-4011: "SmartRouting fallback duplicates with Retrofit suspend adapter on Android 16; add FallbackGuard + cancel-on-fallback + docs" <https://redwood.internal/issue/RED-DEVEX-4011>

omar_b: one more ask: add an e2e that simulates flaky network + fallback to prevent regressions. Also include a small test that verifies idempotency header bytes are identical across clones.

leah_y: adding both tests in the PR. Will include note: "If you rely on server dedupe, ensure server canonicalizes idempotency token independent of chunking/transfer encoding."

sam_k: perfect. Long-term product thought: maybe SmartRouting should prefer 307-style redirect semantics instead of re-issuing POSTs so browsers/clients with strict transfer encoding preserve identity. But that's bigger. For now shipping FallbackGuard + docs is the right path.

leah_y: thanks all — PR up for review :rocket:
